nodes.label: Events Model
nodes.rationale: Events are not mosque-only: Location and Organizer are two independent optional links and must never be coupled. Location has three tiers (existing place, OSM/Digitransit pick, or custom Google Maps link resolved server-side via enrichPendingEventRows()); Organizer is free text optionally tied to a directory place_id. Rendering/filtering must never assume ev.placeId is set and must fall back to locationName/locationAddress/lat/lng.

nodes.label: Maps Link Enrichment (parseMapsUrl/resolveUrl)
nodes.rationale: Code.gs must handle every Google Maps share-link format. Mobile maps.app.goo.gl links resolve to ?q=...&ftid=0xHEX:0xHEX whose second hex segment is the place CID and must be BigInt hex->decimal converted (it exceeds Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) into cid:<decimal>, else enrichment silently degrades to bare geocoding. resolveUrl()'s body-text fallback must decode \uXXXX escapes and not swallow the closing escaped quote; debug with testResolveMapsLink() before guessing.

nodes.label: HSL Trunk Bus Styling
nodes.rationale: Special HUD treatment: HSL trunk buses use the orange trunk colour instead of the standard blue transit colour.

nodes.label: Maneuver Icons
nodes.rationale: Turn-by-turn instruction icons shown inside the HUD's teal square, reusing the app's existing SVGs; teal for direct modes, mode-coloured for transit boarding, arrive/pin icon when alighting.

nodes.label: Transit Navigation Modes
nodes.rationale: HUD states for transit journeys: walking leg to/from a stop, boarding a vehicle (bus/tram/metro/train/ferry) with a prominent route-number chip, and alighting at the destination stop.

nodes.label: Design D — Compact Chip Bar
nodes.rationale: Full-width pill with route name, info chips, and a nav pill; the most compact, data-dense option.

nodes.label: Design H — Dark Ticker Bar
nodes.rationale: Dark pill inverted from the map with inline route + duration; bold, high-contrast, app-like.

nodes.label: Design E — Elevated Tag Card
nodes.rationale: Two-row white card: route title + close on top, info tag chips + Go pill below; rich info density in a clean frame.

nodes.label: Design F — Segmented Rule Bar
nodes.rationale: Pill split into segments by thin dividers, each chunk with one job (mode, route, duration, actions); structured and scannable.

nodes.label: Design B — Surface Card + Accent Edge
nodes.rationale: White card with a teal left accent stripe and a labeled nav pill; clean, neutral, readable.

nodes.label: Design C — Two-Tone Split

nodes.label: Enhanced Map Pin
nodes.rationale: Animated/glowing map pin whose intensity scales with tier (Basic float, Featured bounce+glow, Spotlight bounce+scale+glow).

nodes.label: Promo Code Button
nodes.rationale: Promo code shown in the popup and surfaced via the Promos pill listing; enabled for Featured and Spotlight tiers only.

nodes.label: Search Ranking Boost
nodes.rationale: Additive score boost applied in search ranking for Featured (+0.15) and Spotlight (+0.25) tiers.

nodes.label: Sponsor Badge (Popup)
nodes.rationale: Gold 'Sponsored ✦' badge pill shown in the place popup next to the place type; identical across all tiers so users cannot tell which tier a sponsor purchased, with an info tooltip disclosing that sponsorship does not influence listing/tagging/reporting.

nodes.label: Sponsor Indicator (List Card)

nodes.label: Sponsored Restaurants Carousel

nodes.label: Sponsorship Tiers (Basic/Featured/Spotlight)
nodes.rationale: Three cumulative tiers; all show the same 'Sponsored ✦' label to users while the tier only gates features behind the scenes (Basic = credibility signal, Featured = promo codes + search boost, Spotlight = maximum exposure incl. carousel and OG sharing).

nodes.label: Verification Email (OTP)
nodes.rationale: Transactional email that displays a 6-digit OTP to confirm the user's email before publishing reviews. Code expires in 10 minutes; includes anti-phishing guidance (ignore if not requested, never share the code). Table-based layout with inline styles and MSO fallback for email-client compatibility; uses the app's teal (#08705B) brand accent.

nodes.rationale: Turn-by-turn navigation heads-up display mockups (Design E, chip-tag layout) covering every transport mode, with a standard teal maneuver icon square and standard close button.

nodes.label: Route Snackbar Designs
nodes.rationale: Design-exploration doc presenting eight alternative layouts (A–H) for the active-route snackbar, trading off familiarity, information density, and app-like decisiveness.

nodes.label: Halal Finder Sponsorship Plan
nodes.rationale: Print-oriented plan proposing a paid restaurant sponsorship program: tiers, per-feature visual specs, data-management columns, ethical safeguards, UX walkthrough, pricing, and implementation summary.

nodes.label: UI Element Reference (Halal Finder Helsinki)
nodes.rationale: Canonical catalog of the app's UI components (20 numbered sections + Color Palette + a 'What You Might Call It → Proper Name' quick-reference table mapping informal names and CSS selectors to the proper component names).

nodes.label: Weekly Report Email
nodes.rationale: Compact analytics digest email (stat tiles for Visits/Users/Contributions/Pending, 4-week average deltas, Country pulse and Contribution breakdown bar charts, Pending review queue card). Localhost traffic is excluded by querying only maps.karamahcollective.com; the 4-week average uses the four weeks before the report window; real email uses inline styles for client compatibility.

nodes.label: Boycott Override
nodes.rationale: Data-management mechanism governing how a place's boycott status interacts with (and takes precedence over) its sponsorship.

nodes.label: Ethical & Transparency Safeguards
nodes.rationale: Guiding principle that sponsorship must not influence how a place is listed, tagged, or reported by the community; enforced by identical labeling across tiers and an explicit disclosure tooltip on the sponsor badge.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Pages Functions
nodes.rationale: Server-side code lives only in functions/ on the V8 Workers runtime (no Node builtins); every response carries CORS via allowedOrigin(); inputs validated with length/size caps; errors return generic JSON without leaking internals; endpoints choose an explicit cache strategy (s-maxage+stale-while-revalidate for /api/places, no-store for /api/config).

nodes.label: Code Quality Standards
nodes.rationale: JSDoc on all exports, no magic numbers (UPPER_SNAKE_CASE constants), _-prefix private module state, no console.log in production, <=100-line functions, ordered imports, custom event names centralised in src/events.js, consistent try/catch in Cloudflare functions, and no dead code. The Architect enforces on new code; the Refactorer brings existing code up to them.

nodes.label: Design System (Tokens + Templates)
nodes.rationale: Token-first and template-first: never hard-code colours/sizes/radii/shadows/transitions; every visual value references a --token from design-tokens.css; styles.css holds only layout/position/unique overrides; visually-identical JS/legacy classes are aliased onto existing template selectors rather than duplicated.

nodes.label: Google Sheets as Database (Apps Script)
nodes.rationale: Per the agent definitions, data lives in a Google Sheet served through a Google Apps Script web app, proxied by /api/places and /api/submit; client JS never queries the Sheet directly. (Note: README states this Apps Script/Sheets backend is retired in favour of Cloudflare D1 — the agent docs are stale on this point.)

nodes.label: Static-Site Hard Constraints
nodes.rationale: Vanilla JS ES modules only, no bundler/framework/SSR, no build step, zero runtime npm deps (Playwright dev-only); Cloudflare Pages free tier (100k invocations/day, 10ms CPU); code ships as-is and must run directly in the browser or the V8 Workers runtime.

nodes.label: Preference Log (cross-session memory)
nodes.rationale: docs/PREFERENCE_LOG.md is read at session start and appended at session end/before deploy to persist decisions, preferences, patterns-to-follow/avoid, and session notes so settled questions are never re-asked.

nodes.label: Security Posture
nodes.rationale: Full CSP/HSTS/X-Frame-Options/Permissions-Policy in _headers; CORS locked to maps.karamahcollective.com; SRI on CDN resources; esc() for all user text in JS-generated HTML; server-side validation authoritative; secrets via config.local.js (gitignored) or Cloudflare env vars; Sec-Fetch-Site gating of /data/*.json and /src/* in _middleware.js.

nodes.label: Weekly Report Endpoint (/api/weekly-report)
nodes.rationale: A Saturday 06:00 UTC cron (plus manual workflow_dispatch) POSTs to the Cloudflare Pages /api/weekly-report endpoint with a Bearer REPORT_SECRET to trigger the weekly Cloudflare analytics email report.

nodes.label: MapLibre GL (CDN, SRI-pinned)
nodes.rationale: MapLibre GL 3.6.2 CSS and JS are loaded from unpkg with SRI integrity hashes and crossorigin — the sole rendering library, no bundler.

nodes.label: Cloudflare D1 Database
nodes.rationale: All mutable data (places, tags, reviews, wishes, events, Eid prayers, submitted edits, account-sync rows, admin metadata) lives in Cloudflare D1, bound to Pages Functions as DB. D1 replaced the legacy Apps Script/Google Sheets backend, which is retired; new contact-form submissions are emailed via Brevo rather than stored.

nodes.label: Service Worker & Caching
nodes.rationale: sw.js pre-caches the app shell and uses a multi-tier stale-while-revalidate strategy (shell, tiles capped 500, glyphs 64, satellite 300); dynamic API calls are network-only. The VERSION constant in sw.js must exactly match the ?v=YYYYMMDD query strings in index.html or the SW skips the update and serves stale files.

nodes.label: Deployment Branch Model (main->preview->deploy)
nodes.rationale: Three branches: main (full repo), preview (curated app-file subset, staging domain), deploy (production copy of preview). Never git push directly to preview/deploy — they are managed only via the promotion steps. 'deploy' intentionally bypasses preview because triggering a preview build is pointless when shipping straight to production; package.json is deliberately excluded from promotion (preview/deploy keep their own minimal one).

nodes.label: Dev-only GPS Sim Deploy Toggle
nodes.rationale: Step 0 of every deploy comments out initGpsSim() in src/app.js (committed to main and promoted), and Step 9 restores it in the working tree only (never staged/committed), so the simulator is available locally yet never ships enabled on main, preview, or deploy.

nodes.label: Firebase Authentication (CDN)
nodes.rationale: firebase-app.js and firebase-auth.js are loaded as external CDN ES modules (gstatic, SRI-pinned) following the same convention as MapLibre; src/auth.js imports the exact same URLs so the browser module cache is reused rather than re-fetched. Identity layer only (Google/Microsoft/Facebook/email-password) — no Firestore.

nodes.label: Menu/Profile Merged Sheet
nodes.rationale: One physical .sheet with two panes (#menu-sheet-body/#profile-sheet-body) reached after 4 iterations: (1) coordinated two-sheet swap wobbled via a height reflow; (2) align-items:stretch removed the wobble but left dead whitespace below the shorter pane; (3) animating #mp-scroll/#mp-pane-track height directly broke scrolling and disabled slide transitions; (4) final design inserts #mp-height-wrap between #mp-scroll and #mp-pane-track so scroll-fit, active-pane height animation, and the slide transform never collide.

nodes.label: Legacy Anonymous OTP Review Flow Retirement
nodes.rationale: Firebase Auth already covers identity end-to-end, so send-otp/verify-otp and the Verifications table are dropped entirely (also removing the only need for a new outbound-email dependency). Historical OTP-submitted review rows still migrate as normal data; only the creation mechanism is retired.
nodes.norm_label: legacy anonymous otp review flow retirement

nodes.label: Reviews Upsert via UNIQUE(place_id, email_hash)
nodes.rationale: Replaces Code.gs's scan-then-branch logic with a single upsert keyed on the (place_id, email_hash) unique constraint.

nodes.label: Hybrid Moderation
nodes.rationale: Star ratings take effect immediately while optional text reviews go to a pending status for admin approval, separating the rating signal from potentially harmful content.

nodes.label: In-app Review System
nodes.rationale: 1-5 star ratings plus optional 20-500 character text reviews, replacing reliance on Google ratings; adds src/reviews.js and functions/api/reviews.js.

nodes.label: Triple-Identity Anti-Abuse
nodes.rationale: Deduplicates on device ID (hf_device_id) plus a SHA-256 browser fingerprint (canvas + WebGL + hardware) plus an IP hash of CF-Connecting-IP; the most aggressive anti-abuse achievable without requiring login.

nodes.label: Raised OTP Rate Limits (testing)
nodes.rationale: During testing OTP_RATE_PER_EMAIL_HOUR is 50 (production 3) and OTP_RATE_PER_IP_HOUR is 100 (production 10).

nodes.label: Pre-deploy Revert Checklist
nodes.rationale: Must revert before any production deploy: the skipped OTP email send, the raised OTP rate limits, the debug field in error responses, the testSendEmail() helper, and the client-side localhost OTP bypass in src/reviews.js.

nodes.label: Edge Firebase ID Token Verification
nodes.rationale: Verify Firebase ID tokens at the edge via JWKS RS256 using Web Crypto (functions/_firebase-verify.js), with no server SDK, keeping the app on Cloudflare's V8 runtime.

nodes.label: Audit Log Table
nodes.rationale: audit_log table added to schema.sql as a documented, intentional exception to the emailHash-only rule; a generic audit-log hook fires on every admin write action.

nodes.label: authenticateAdmin() Firebase Domain Gate
nodes.rationale: Retires the adminKey and gates /api/admin on a Firebase ID token plus emailVerified plus an @karamahcollective.com domain check.

nodes.label: Separate Admin Cloudflare Pages Project
nodes.rationale: The admin/ dashboard deploys as its own Pages project (halal-finder-admin) at admin.maps.karamahcollective.com; it needs admin/wrangler.toml with pages_build_output_dir='dist' so Cloudflare does not walk up to the repo-root wrangler.toml.

nodes.label: Conventional Commits Format
nodes.rationale: Format <type>(<scope>): <subject>. Use ci(release) for version bumps and data refreshes, ci(deploy) for branch promotions to production, and chore only for zero-user-impact tooling.

nodes.label: Promotion-based Deploy (deploy/preview branches)
nodes.rationale: Cloudflare Pages here builds only the deploy (production) and preview branches, not arbitrary pushed branches. Changes reach them by promoting curated files via git checkout <source> -- <file-list>, deliberately excluding package.json and wrangler.toml, which each branch keeps its own copy of.

nodes.label: Button Templates
nodes.rationale: Fully-rounded pill buttons with color/opacity/filter feedback only (no size or transform on hover/press); buttons are either icon-only or text-only, with documented exceptions.

nodes.label: Plus Jakarta Sans Typeface
nodes.rationale: Project typeface replacing Inter/General Sans; high x-height, crisp ClearType hinting, self-hosted with latin and latin-ext subsets for Finnish characters.

nodes.label: Reduce Motion Single-source Mechanism
nodes.rationale: A single JS-computed html.reduce-motion class, fed by a localStorage override else the live matchMedia value, so every motion check in CSS and JS reads one source of truth instead of a parallel bare @media block.

nodes.label: showConfirmDialog() Confirmation Pattern
nodes.rationale: One reusable Yes/No dialog (showConfirmDialog() plus .confirm-overlay/.confirm-card) replaces the now-obsolete press-twice-to-confirm pattern for review delete and sign-out.

nodes.label: Template-first CSS / Component Alias Pattern
nodes.rationale: Every visual pattern must exist as a reusable class in design-tokens.css before being used in styles.css or JS; a JS class that is visually identical to a template is added to the template selector as an alias rather than duplicated.

nodes.label: Third-party Brand Button Exception
nodes.rationale: Third-party brand buttons (e.g. .btn-google) follow the vendor's own official button spec over the app palette, using dedicated --google-btn-* tokens; the recognizability and trust of a well-known brand mark outweighs internal color consistency for that one component.

nodes.label: 'Premium Utility' Design Vision
nodes.rationale: Clean, airy, generous spacing, dramatic typography hierarchy, and consistent radii and animations across components; flat and minimal with very subtle shadows, never glassy, blurry, or HUD-like.

nodes.label: Firebase Authentication
nodes.rationale: Firebase Auth as the identity layer: Google, Microsoft, email magic-link and email/password sign-in; no Firestore. Project 'Halal Map Karamah' (halal-map-karamah).

nodes.label: Place-detail Bottom Sheet
nodes.rationale: showPlacePopup() becomes openPlaceSheet() rendering into #place-sheet, reusing the .sheet template and initSheetDrag.

nodes.label: Two-way Cross-device Reconcile
nodes.rationale: A 'known synced' localStorage baseline (hf_sync_known_v1) lets the merge distinguish a genuinely new local item from a previously-synced item removed elsewhere, enabling deletion propagation across signed-in devices; an offline-removal resurrection edge case is acknowledged as residual.

nodes.label: Merged Menu/Profile Sheet
nodes.rationale: A single #menu-sheet holds two panes on #mp-pane-track, switched by _setActivePane with _syncPaneHeight height syncing.

nodes.label: Sheet Animation Utilities
nodes.rationale: animateElementHeight(), crossFadeSwap() and initSheetDrag() in src/utils.js drive sheet height animation, pane cross-fades and drag-to-dismiss.

nodes.label: Email Hash Privacy Principle
nodes.rationale: Store emailHash = sha256(verified email), never the plaintext email, as the account and review identity key, so no personal email is persisted.

nodes.label: Mosque Dome Emblem
nodes.rationale: Dome iconography signals a Muslim / halal-focused product at a glance, establishing immediate cultural relevance for a halal-finding service.

nodes.label: Gold & Deep-Purple Brand Palette
nodes.rationale: Gold conveys a premium, traditional feel evoking mosque ornamentation; the deep-purple wordmark provides high-contrast, modern legibility against the cream ground; symmetric centered composition reinforces a formal, trustworthy identity.

nodes.label: Cloudflare D1 Database
nodes.rationale: Chosen because the app is already 100% Cloudflare Pages: D1 binds directly into the existing Functions with zero extra network hop, and its free tier covers current and near-future scale. It replaces the slow external Apps Script HTTP hop and its public, unauthenticated exec URL.

nodes.label: D1 Schema (14 tables)
nodes.rationale: 14 tables plus indexes; the Verifications table is intentionally dropped because Firebase Auth now covers identity.

nodes.label: Server-side Nominatim Geocoding
nodes.rationale: Server-side enrichment reuses the free, keyless OpenStreetMap Nominatim endpoint the app already calls client-side instead of GAS Maps.newGeocoder(), so the migration needs zero new third-party vendor signups.

nodes.label: Google Sheets to Cloudflare D1 Migration Plan
nodes.norm_label: google sheets to cloudflare d1 migration plan

nodes.label: ON CONFLICT Partial-Index Match Requirement
nodes.rationale: SQLite requires an ON CONFLICT target to repeat a partial unique index's WHERE clause exactly (idx_saved_places_placeid_kinds WHERE kind IN ('favorite','visited')) or it throws 'ON CONFLICT clause does not match any PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint' instead of matching.

nodes.label: Brand Teal Accent + Neutral Surfaces
nodes.rationale: Brand teal #08705B replaces blue as --accent; all surfaces are pure neutral grays (the warm #FDFCF8 is explicitly rejected); AMOLED-black (#000000) dark mode and pure-white light mode with no warm tint on any surface.

nodes.label: Hook Pattern for Circular Module Dependencies
nodes.rationale: When module A needs module B but B already imports A, export a setHooks() from A and call it from B at evaluation time to register callbacks, avoiding import cycles.
nodes.norm_label: hook pattern for circular module dependencies

nodes.label: Navigation Camera Model
nodes.rationale: Three discrete zoom/pitch tiers (standard cruising, full turn zoom, highway zoom-out), not a continuous curve; heading derived from route polyline geometry (immune to GPS jitter), GPS-centered follow via a rAF jumpTo loop, always-follow with any manual pan breaking follow instantly.

nodes.label: No Automated Tests Without Explicit Ask
nodes.rationale: Standing rule (2026-08-02): do not run Playwright or any test suite unless the user explicitly asks; a node --check syntax pass is fine but a browser verification pass is not. The user tests every change manually in a real browser.
nodes.norm_label: no automated tests without explicit ask

nodes.label: config.local.js Secret Injection
nodes.rationale: Secrets live in git-ignored src/config.local.js for local dev; on Cloudflare Pages, scripts/build-secrets.js generates that file from environment variables at build time, so the repository can be public without exposing any secrets.

nodes.label: DT_API_KEY (Digitransit key)
nodes.rationale: The only API requiring a subscription key; the same key authenticates both the HSL and Waltti Digitransit routing endpoints.

nodes.label: External Routing/Geocoding APIs
nodes.rationale: HSL and Waltti Digitransit, Nominatim, OSRM, Transitous and Overpass; only Digitransit needs a key, the rest are public/keyless.

nodes.label: Static-site / Zero-dependency Architecture
nodes.rationale: Static site only: no bundler, SSR or frameworks; vanilla JS ES modules; zero runtime dependencies (Playwright dev-only); all server logic in functions/ on V8 Web APIs. React and any framework are explicitly rejected.
